meta.project: Flow — get the whole app working end to end (Flutter UI + Rust daemon) on Windows
meta.goal: All UI buttons work and show correct info; no mock/placeholder data leaking into the shipped UI; two daemons discover + pair through the Flutter UI; tray icon behaves correctly; no crashes; graceful shutdown on every close path.
workingStateCriteria: Every button in the shipped Flutter app is clickable, fires a real daemon command, and reflects the real result.
No hardcoded/mock/placeholder data rendered as fact anywhere in the shipped UI.
Daemon-to-daemon discovery and pairing completes through the Flutter UI (two instances on this machine, and on a second physical machine if available).
Tray icon: correct tooltip, left-click toggles window, right-click menu works, Quit actually quits.
No panics/crashes in daemon or Flutter across normal use, startup races, mid-session daemon death, and restart.
Window close, tray Quit, and Ctrl-C on the daemon all shut down gracefully with no lingering processes.
meta.howToUseThisFile: Update each task's status as work lands. Add a 'note' with what was actually done / verified how. Keep this in sync with the in-session todo list.

tracks.title: Multi-instance support (run two daemon+UI instances on one machine)
tracks.note: VERIFIED: two flow-daemon instances run side-by-side on this Windows box (A on 47823, B on 47833, shared discovery 47824), discover each other over UDP broadcast, and complete a real Noise-authenticated daemon-to-daemon pairing end to end via IPC — both sides persist each other as paired devices and both link states go to 'connected'. Driven headlessly with flutter/tool/ipc_poke.dart.

tasks.title: Daemon: FLOW_IPC_PORT env override for the IPC listener + advertised port
tasks.note: main.rs: ipc_port() reads FLOW_IPC_PORT (unparseable = fatal, not silent fallback). Peer-channel port is already ephemeral+advertised, so nothing else to do there.

tasks.title: Daemon: FLOW_DATA_DIR env override for the SQLite DB + identity (separate per instance)
tasks.note: main.rs: db_path() honors FLOW_DATA_DIR; separate dir => separate flow.db + separate persisted ed25519 identity.

tasks.title: Daemon: FLOW_IPC_TOKEN_PATH env override for the IPC auth token file
tasks.note: ipc/auth.rs: token_path() honors FLOW_IPC_TOKEN_PATH. Also replaced directories::BaseDirs with a USERPROFILE(Windows)/HOME(else) resolver matching the Flutter client's ipc_auth.dart exactly, so both sides compute the identical ~/.flow path and the 2 pre-existing Windows-only auth test failures are fixed.

tasks.title: Daemon: SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT on the discovery UDP socket so two instances share port 47824
tasks.note: discovery/tcp.rs: bind_reusable_udp() via socket2 sets SO_REUSEADDR (+SO_REUSEPORT on unix) before bind. Verified: 2 instances both bind 47824 and both receive broadcast announces on Windows. Added socket2 dep.

tasks.title: Flutter: FLOW_IPC_PORT + FLOW_IPC_TOKEN_PATH dart-defines wired into ipc_constants.dart / ipc_auth.dart
tasks.note: ipc_constants.dart: kFlowDaemonIpcPortResolved from int.fromEnvironment. ipc_auth.dart: _envTokenPath from String.fromEnvironment + Windows-first USERPROFILE resolution.

tasks.title: Unit tests for the override plumbing; confirm default path unchanged
tasks.note: New: discovery two_instances_can_share_one_fixed_discovery_port; auth flow_ipc_token_path_overrides_the_default_location; main ipc_port_defaults_and_overrides. Also fixed pre-existing clippy -D warnings failure (dead futures_util::StreamExt import in ipc/server.rs tests) and made auth tests share one ENV_LOCK. cargo test --workspace + clippy --all-targets -D warnings + fmt --check all green.

tasks.title: BONUS: FLOW_DEVICE_NAME override + kill unprompted pairing-handshake churn
tasks.note: service/mod.rs: FLOW_DEVICE_NAME overrides local_hostname() so two instances on one machine are distinguishable. dial_if_trusted now early-outs when TrustGate::has_any_trusted() is false (was doing a full TCP+Noise handshake against every discovered peer every 5s); the 'no pairing session open' log dropped WARN->debug (it's routine, not a fault).
